title: Hearth of Thorns
shortDescription: Living briar holds the glass and the light.
longDescription:
The Hearth of Thorns is half cloister and half greenhouse. Briar has been trained into trellises that remember every cut, and green light pools on the stone like water held in a leaf. Shears hang where a first-year can reach them and a second-year has learned not to rush. The air smells of crushed sap, damp earth, and the faint sweetness of something flowering out of season.
Mentor Briar waits among the living walls as if the plants had asked her to stay.

fixtures.name: Mentor Briar
fixtures.lookDescription: A scarred hedgehog in a green cloak caught with thorns, shears at the belt. Try talk briar.
fixtures.examineDescription: Briar's quills are patched with old scratches. The cloak is mended with vine-thread. She speaks as if the plants were listening, and they usually are.
fixtures.dialogue: "Thorns teach patience that can still cut. Look this hearth — the living wood, the tied new growth. Find Flint in the South Orchard. Come back when the dummy has taught you something honest."

welcome.text: "I am Briar. Mind the thorns as you come in — they are trained, not cruel, but they do not make exceptions for hurry. Thorns grow where they are asked to grow. Look this hearth. See how the living wood has been tied, not broken. Then walk to the South Orchard, where fallen blossom collects along the paths and Flint keeps a dummy in a straw hat. Attack it once. Return and talk to me. The plants will still be listening when you get back."

craft.text: "A vine that is never cut becomes a snare. A vine that is only cut becomes a stick. You will learn the difference — when to ask, when to prune, when to let a thing keep its thorns. First you look. Then you practice on Flint's dummy, which is meant to be struck and will not hold a grudge. Then you come back, and we will see whether you noticed the new growth or only the old scars."

go.text: "Look the trellis. Ask before you cut, even with your eyes. Then find the orchard south of Lantern Court. I will be here among the living walls."

lessons-done.text: "You have looked. You have stood in the orchard, and the dummy has already forgotten you, as good practice should. Thorns have your name, and your kit is open. Alder waits in the High Study with a question about the bell below — an old abbey note that the timber still carries. Go up when you are ready. Do not rush the stair. The plants never do."

fixtures.name: Briar Trellis
fixtures.examineDescription: The living wood has been trained into a door that is also a warning. New growth is tied, not broken. A slate says: 'Ask before you cut.'
